answer.evidence: This is an office chair seen from behind. The backrest (rows 5-14) is a flat blue panel with a 1-row highlight at row 7 and no top plane. The seat is a light band of only 2 rows (15-16, L=148), followed by a dark vertical face (rows 17-22, L=61) and an outline at row 23. The seat band is only a rim-like 2 rows with no eave shadow, so it matches the 'seat: band 2' wrong reference rather than a 5-row seat top. The pole (rows 24-25) and the base and wheels (rows 26-30) are small supports. The whole object reads as a front elevation without a real seat surface seen from above.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small blue-grey office chair. Its outlines are tinted dark blue rather than black, which matches Beodeul practice (only 10% of dark edge pixels are neutral). Its 13 colours are on par with the bench (14) and hedge (11), and its median of 10 colours per tile equals the hedge's. The weaknesses are in the shading and fills. The backrest and seat cushion have only about 4 lightness steps, against 5-6 on the references. Flat-fill coverage is 22%, higher than every reference (0-13%), so the backrest and seat read as broad, nearly uniform panels with little grain or per-part highlighting. Next to the richer pieces (cheese stall with 40 colours, well with 38) it looks flatter and closer to a clean sticker. It is cleanly drawn but not at the reference's craft level, so it fails on the doubt rule.

surfaces.part: backrest (seen from behind, top edge band)

answer.evidence: The chair faces north, so we see its back. The upper blue block (rows 5-14) is a wide seat surface seen from above. It has a lighter back-edge highlight on row 7 and a dark front-edge outline on row 14. Below it, the backrest (rows 15-23) has a light 2-row top edge band (rows 15-16) over a darker vertical face (rows 17-22). Armrests show as dark side strips in rows 8-16. Below that, a stem (rows 24-25) and a caster base (rows 26-30) give the support structure. The seat top is 9-10 rows and the front face is 9 rows or more, so the main body has both a top and a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The outline is fine: only 10% of dark edge pixels are neutral, and the dark navy lean matches the blue chair body, like Beodeul's tinted outlines. Shading and texture are weaker. The backrest and seat are smooth blue slabs with about 4 lightness steps (highlight, base, shade, deep), against about 5-6 on the references. Flat-fill coverage is 22%, above every reference (0% for bench, hedge, lamp and well; 13% for the stall), which shows in the plain backrest and seat panels with no grain, stitching dots or per-form variation. Per-tile median is 10 colours, equal to the hedge, but the candidate has only 13 distinct colours in total. The base and wheels are small and simple. A careful artist would find it a bit flatter and more sticker-like than the bench, well or stall, so it narrowly fails the bar.
